answer: Back each agent with a company director's registry record. The agent cites its company number; validators pull a signed extract from the business registry, confirm the firm is active with filed accounts, and store a salted hash of the director's registry ID. A string of shell firms threaded like a pearl necklace still maps to one director hash, so splitting gains nothing; each extra agent needs a new real director who passes the registry's ID check and pays yearly fees. Limit: a crook may wander to lax registries abroad, so that voyage across jurisdictions needs per-country trust weights.
